newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issues flow, some spreads softer.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issues flow, some spreads softer.

text.p: Distribution of about $2.5 billion high-grade bonds was the top priority for U.S. corporate bond market on Tuesday, and spreads were flat to wider in lackluster secondary activity, dealers said.

Dealers told success stories of the deals, which included $550 million multi-tranche debt from Mead Corp, $500 million 10-year debt Philip Morris Cos Inc, and a $700 million first-time debt issue from paint-maker Sherwin-Williams Co.
Still, the issuance after a busy January and talk of more of the same this month led some traders to forecast more spread softening, albeit slight.

"Spreads held in today because there was very little activity," said one industrials trader. "But we're starting to lose a little ground. You'll see them widen out when you see activity pick up a little more."
Further, some dealers noted highly rated issues were priced at the cheaper side of price talk.

Philip Morris' $500 million A2/single-A rated notes, which priced as 7.20s to yield 7.343 percent, came at 78 basis points over the Treasury curve compared with talk in the range of 76 to 78 basis points. The deal sold well as Treasuries ran higher, a trader said.
Elsewhere, Sherwin-Williams Co issued $700 million A2/single-A debt in a five-part public and private offering. Traders called the deal "attractively priced."

The public debt was priced at yields ranging from 25 basis points over Treasuries in three years to 63 basis points over the T-bond for 30-year debt. An attached 144a offering was priced to yield 63 basis points over in 30-years and 73 basis points over (T-bond) for $150 million century bonds.
Mead Corp's $550 multi-tranche A3/A-minus debt was on the rich side, some traders said, but neither did they expect much widening when the bonds are freed to trade on Wednesday.
Mead's issue was priced at spreads of 38 basis points over for five-year debt and 40put10s, 58 over for 20-year debt and 80 over for 50-year bonds.
Elsewhere, Export-Import Bank of Korea issued $500 million A1/AA-minus rated five-year global bonds at 45 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Trust preferreds also continued to pound the market with supply ahead of the delivery of President Clinton's budget proposal. Secondary trust preferred spreads were softer.
Turning to high-yielders, talk of a burgeoning forward calendar also captured the focus on Tuesday.

In secondary market trading, traders said prices were firmer across the board but actual volume was relatively light. However, Farm Fresh Inc debt fell more than four points following the resignation of its Chief Executive Officer and downgrade of the company's senior notes to Caa from B3.
Moody's Investors Service said the resignation and absence of credible restructuring plan prompted the downgrade.

New high-yield issuance was light on Tuesday ahead of what could be $5 billion of supply through February. Those numbers still failed to raise eyebrows, traders said, based on the fabulous string of monthly cash inflows to mutual funds.
Rio Hotel & Casino Inc issued $125 million B2/single-B rated 10-year senior subordinated notes as 9-1/2s to yield 314 basis points over Treasuries on Tuesday.
Rio Hotel Chairman Anthony A. Marnell II said the company issued the debt to refinance amounts outstanding under a $200 million bank credit line.

In the Treasury market, the two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee essentially dampened activity. Prices gravitated higher as the FOMC was widely expected to leave rates unchanged when the meeting adjourns on Wednesday.
The 30-year bond closed up 13/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
